_: AUTHORED — 46 decisions, one per rail, made by reading each chain and asking which published criterion it ANSWERS. Not derived from the card's topic, and deliberately not derived at all: criterion-tagging-traps is the record of what a regex does here — it files a card by its distractors, decides the primary by rule order, and matches bare words inside other words. A rail is a chain of ideas with no stem and no options, which is the WORST possible input to a text matcher and the easiest for a human. apply-migration.mjs fails if any rail is missing from this table, if a key matches no rail, or if a value is not a criterion of the pack.
_scope: PRIMARY ONLY. No alsoCrit is set here. Ring membership, the thin round, every count on the Checklist and the coverage arithmetic all read these tags, so one tag per rail keeps the change auditable — 46 rails, 46 decisions, and nothing else moves. Several chains genuinely touch a second criterion (the artery wall reaches peripheral resistance; the chemoreflex reaches ventilation); adding those is a separate pass with its own evidence.
_thin: Rails still do not count toward coverage. perPoint() in the engine skips type:'rail' and background.thin is computed before the rails are appended, so 'thin' keeps meaning 'how much of HER material exists here'. What these tags buy is that every card in the pack is filed under a checklist item — which was literally false for 46 of 434 — and that a rail on a thin point is now dealt in the round that says its cards are load-bearing, instead of last, as optional background.
